card.name: Verbs like present after can or may
card.fires_on: The verb "present" (and sometimes "occur") right after a modal such as "can" or "may" when describing how a condition shows up clinically. It also fires on "urrent" in "Recurrent Pericarditis".

modes.label: Condition may present
modes.description: "present" after can/may, introducing how a disease shows up.
modes.example: FDE may<< present>> as a more severe variant known as generalized

modes.label: Event may occur
modes.description: "occur" after may or to, describing when or how often an effect happens.

card.writes: It promotes words that continue a description of a clinical presentation, such as "presentation" and "ritten".
card.plain: It marks the verb that says how a condition shows up or when an effect happens.
